home.title: Run your immigration practice in one secure workspace
home.subtitle: Clients, files, IRCC questionnaires, documents, booking, and portals — built for Canadian immigration work, not generic CRM.
home.ctaNote: Free during open testing. No credit card required.
home.featuresTitle: Everything your firm needs to move files forward
home.featuresSubtitle: Replace scattered spreadsheets, email threads, and ad-hoc portals with a practice system designed around immigration files.

projects.title: Immigration projects
projects.body: Open a file once: program family, jurisdiction, status, participants, and the forms checklist seeded for that pathway.

people.title: Lifelong client records
people.body: Keep clients as durable records across engagements — contact details, history, notes, and linked projects in one place.

forms.title: Ask-once questionnaires
forms.body: Clients answer once. Your team uses those answers to prepare IRCC forms, including IMM 5476 representative details.

share.title: Secure client links
share.body: Send a time-limited link for forms and document upload. Regenerate access without losing answers already collected.

booking.title: Booking and calendar
booking.body: Publish consultation services, take public bookings, and sync busy times with Google Calendar and Meet when you connect it.

portal.title: Client portal access
portal.body: Give clients a firm-branded way back into their file with access codes and passwords handled on the server, not in the browser.

team.title: Firm workspace
team.body: Each consulting firm gets its own tenant. Staff sign in with email or Google and work inside firm-scoped data.

languages.title: Built bilingual
languages.body: Work in English, French, or Spanish — for your team and for the client-facing flows they use.

one.title: Create the project
one.body: Add participants inline, pick the program, and seed the forms checklist in one screen.

two.title: Collect once
two.body: Share a secure link so clients upload documents and complete the questionnaire.

three.title: Prepare and track
three.body: Your firm reviews answers, fills forms, books follow-ups, and keeps status visible.

home.securitySubtitle: Clients trust you with passports, biographies, and family details. We designed Yuzu Immigration so your firm can meet that trust with clear, practical safeguards.

canada.title: Primary data in Canada
canada.body: Database, authentication, and file storage run on Supabase in Canada (AWS Canada Central).

encryption.title: Encryption that matches the risk
encryption.body: TLS in transit, infrastructure encryption at rest, and firm-level AES-256-GCM for uploaded documents and many identity fields.

access.title: Your firm’s data stays yours
access.body: Access is scoped to each organization. Public booking and share links use unguessable tokens with rate limits and expiry where configured.

privacy.title: Privacy you can explain
privacy.body: Written to support PIPEDA accountability, with closed-file retention tools aligned to typical CICC six-year duties — not a certification, and not legal advice.

home.finalSubtitle: Set up your firm workspace in minutes and see whether it fits how you already practice.
home.finalNote: Free during the open testing phase.

legal.disclaimer: Private immigration portal. Not affiliated with Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) or Ministère de l'Immigration, de la Francisation et de l'Intégration (MIFI).
legal.privacyIntro: Yuzu Immigration is practice-management software operated by Yuzu Solutions for Canadian immigration consultants. This policy describes how personal information is collected, used, disclosed, and protected when you use Yuzu Immigration — including the consultant workspace, client share links, the client portal, and public booking pages. It is written to support PIPEDA accountability. It is not a certification, and it is not legal advice.
legal.consentSummary: Your personal information and documents are shared so this firm can prepare and manage your immigration file in Yuzu Immigration.
legal.consentBody: By continuing, you provide personal information and documents so this consulting firm can prepare and manage your immigration file in Yuzu Immigration. Primary records are stored in Canada. Uploaded files and many identity fields are encrypted. The firm’s staff can open the file in their workspace; Yuzu Solutions processes it to operate the platform. Email, calendar, and hosting details are in our Privacy Policy.

controller.title: 1. Who is responsible
controller.body:
Your consulting firm (the organization with a Yuzu Immigration workspace) decides why and how client personal information is processed for its immigration services. That firm is generally responsible for the client file.

Yuzu Solutions operates the software and processes that information on the firm’s instructions as a service provider. Yuzu Solutions is responsible for staff account information we use to run the service (name, email, and authentication identifiers).

If you book an appointment or complete a form through a firm’s link, you are giving information to that firm. Yuzu Solutions hosts and processes it so the firm can use Yuzu Immigration.

purposes.title: 2. Purposes
purposes.body:
We process personal information to:
• Provide the CRM, questionnaires, form preparation, document intake, share links, client portal, calendar, and public booking features
• Authenticate staff and, where a firm enables it, client portal access
• Send appointment confirmations, change/cancel links, and reminder emails the firm configures
• Sync busy times and bookings with a consultant’s Google Calendar when that consultant connects it
• Maintain security, prevent booking abuse, keep audit records, and operate the service
• Meet legal obligations that apply to Yuzu Solutions as a service provider

We do not sell personal information. We do not use client file contents for advertising.

collection.title: 3. What we collect
collection.body:
Depending on how the product is used, this may include:

Staff and firm: name, email, role, representative profile fields used on IMM 5476, authentication identifiers, the firm’s default language, and — if a consultant connects Google Calendar — that Google account email.

Clients and booking guests: first name, last name, email, phone, address (when asked at booking), preferred language, immigration-status fields a firm records, questionnaire answers, extra questions a firm adds to a booking form, uploaded supporting documents, consultation notes, and generated form files.

Bookings: appointment time, service, consultant, when privacy notice was accepted, Google Meet join links when created, and hashed email and IP used only to rate-limit the public booking page.

Calendar sync (only if a consultant connects Google Calendar): encrypted OAuth tokens, busy intervals, and event titles from that calendar so the firm can see when the consultant is busy. New bookings are written to that calendar with the guest’s name, email, and phone in the event details.

Technical: security audit events (including IP address and browser user-agent for some actions), hashed IP and email for booking abuse control (about 14 days), and anonymous product usage and performance metrics.

Firms should collect only what they need for the engagement. Extra booking questions are stored with the appointment.

legalBasis.title: 4. Consent and notice
legalBasis.body:
Firms are responsible for obtaining meaningful consent from clients where required, and for explaining their own retainers and privacy practices — including Québec Law 25 duties where those apply.

Client share links require a privacy checkbox when the client first sets a password for the link. Public booking requires a checkbox linking to this policy before a booking can be submitted. Checking either box is consent to the processing described here for that firm’s file or appointment, subject to the firm’s instructions and applicable law.

You may refuse by not using the link or not booking. You may ask the firm to withdraw consent or delete information, subject to professional retention rules. Some processing (security logs and legal retention) may continue where the law allows.

safeguards.title: 5. Safeguards
safeguards.body:
We apply safeguards proportionate to the sensitivity of immigration files, including:
• Encryption in transit (TLS)
• Infrastructure encryption at rest for the database, authentication, and file storage
• Application-level AES-256-GCM for uploaded client documents and for many client fields (names, emails, phones, notes, questionnaire answers, booking guest details, and similar), using a separate encryption key per firm
• Some operational fields are stored without that application-level encryption (for example preferred language, immigration-status labels, appointment times, and security audit metadata)
• Access controls scoped to each firm; assistants only see projects they are shared on
• Database service-role privileges restricted to server-only paths
• Public booking and share links identified by unguessable tokens; booking rate limits use hashed email and IP
• Staff passwords handled by Supabase Auth; client portal passwords stored in a private schema and verified only on the server

Yuzu personnel who hold the platform wrap key can technically decrypt firm keys in order to operate and restore the service. We limit that access operationally. No method of transmission or storage is perfectly secure.

retention.title: 6. Retention
retention.body:
Client and project records remain while the firm’s workspace is active. When a file is closed, the product sets a retain-until date of six years after closure to support typical College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants closed-file duties.

Deleting a person or a project from the workspace erases that record’s personal information in the application: identity and contact fields, notes, uploaded documents, questionnaire answers, share links, portal access, and linked bookings (including an attempt to delete the matching Google Calendar event). People who remain on another file at the firm are kept. After the retain-until date, a firm administrator can destroy a closed file the same way. A placeholder project row and an encrypted destruction-register entry (client name and service summary) are kept for the firm’s professional record. Security audit rows for that file or person are kept as a record that the action occurred, with IP address, user agent, and event metadata removed.

Hashed booking abuse events are deleted after about 14 days, and are also removed for an erased person’s email.

Emails already sent, copies of calendar events held by Google, and database backups or point-in-time recovery copies can outlive an application delete until those copies expire. Firms remain responsible for their professional retention and secure-destruction duties.

sharing.title: 7. Sharing and service providers
sharing.body:
We use these providers to run Yuzu Immigration:
• Supabase (Canada) — database, authentication, and file storage
• Vercel — application hosting, Web Analytics, and Speed Insights
• Resend — transactional email when mail sending is configured (confirmations, reminders, and manage links)
• Google — only if a staff member uses Google to sign in, or a consultant connects Google Calendar (OAuth, calendar events, and Google Meet)

Those providers process the information we send them to provide their service. We do not disclose client file contents to third parties for their marketing. We may disclose information if required by law, to protect rights and security, or on the firm’s instructions (for example sending a reminder the firm wrote).

When a consultant connects Google Calendar, Google receives the booking details the product writes to that calendar (including guest name, email, and phone), and we receive busy times and event titles from that calendar.

transfers.title: 8. Location of processing
transfers.body:
Primary application data (database, authentication, and stored files) is hosted in Canada (AWS Canada Central, via Supabase).

The application is hosted on Vercel. Compute, logs, Web Analytics, and Speed Insights may be processed outside Canada, including in the United States.

Transactional email via Resend, and Google sign-in or Google Calendar/Meet when used, are processed by those providers outside Canada.

If you are in Québec, some personal information may therefore be communicated outside Québec. Firms remain responsible for their own transfer assessments where Law 25 requires them.

cookies.title: 9. Cookies and usage data
cookies.body:
Essential cookies store a signed-in session (staff or client portal) and a few interface preferences, such as whether the sidebar is collapsed. The language of the page comes from the URL.

Vercel Web Analytics and Speed Insights collect anonymous page-view and performance data to help us operate the product. They are not used to sell advertising.

rights.title: 10. Your rights
rights.body:
Subject to PIPEDA and other applicable law, individuals may request access to, correction of, deletion of, or information about the handling of their personal information.

Clients and booking guests should normally contact the consulting firm first. Guests can also use the change or cancel links in their confirmation email while those links are valid. Firm administrators may use in-product export tools (person JSON export and project file ZIP) and, where professional retention allows, delete a person or destroy a closed file. Deletion in the product is described in section 6.

You may also contact Yuzu Solutions using the details below. You may complain to the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada, and in Québec to the Commission d’accès à l’information.

breach.title: 11. Breaches
breach.body: If we become aware of a privacy breach, we will assess whether it creates a real risk of significant harm. Where the law requires, we will notify affected organizations and individuals and report to the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada, and we will give firms information they need for their own notices.

children.title: 12. Children and dependents
children.body: The service may store information about minors when they are part of an immigration file. Firms must ensure collection is necessary and appropriately authorized by a parent, guardian, or as otherwise permitted by law.

changes.title: 13. Changes to this policy
changes.body: We may update this policy to reflect product, legal, or security changes. The “Last updated” date will change when we do. Material changes will be highlighted in-product or by notice to firm administrators when practical.

contact.title: 14. Contact
contact.body:
Privacy inquiries for the Yuzu Immigration platform:
Yuzu Solutions — privacy@yuzusolutions.ca

If you are a client of a consulting firm, contact that firm for requests about your immigration file or booking.
